upheld.reason: Supplier Statement names its positive part count m≥1 and total n in N; local F5 renames these d≥1 and M in N. Thus the weak-composition formula includes M=0 exactly as the supplier does. The supplier extra n≥1 restriction belongs only to positive compositions, which F5 never invokes. Steps 1.2 and 3.1 use only finite weak-composition levels.

The first clause of F2 addresses x,y on the closed bounded interval and cites the AC-representative lemma. The second clause explicitly restricts x to [0,L], and the final clause explicitly says on the half-line; its tail window (x,x+1) therefore has x≥0, as in this supplier. No half-line inequality is asserted for arbitrary negative x.

Statement uses the angular-radial unitary U whose labels are l≥0,-l≤m≤l, and explicitly defines V_l only for l≥0. F10 uses its already-defined normalized Y_lm, so the sphere-basis label restriction remains in force; the polar integral identity itself is for every nonnegative Borel g and has no angular label.

Current Statement explicitly says for every l≥0 let A_l be the radial operator of the supplier, and Given identifies l,m as the integer angular labels of U. F2 describes those same A_l,V_l and their domains; it creates no radial operator or eigenfunction for negative l. Steps 2.1–2.2 use these fixed nonnegative labels.
